blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Charge call to the payment provider has no timeout) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge, on every error) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-3 (Charge failures are swallowed without any log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit `timeout=` (connect and read) to `requests.post`. Without it, when the provider accepts the connection but never answers, `requests` waits indefinitely: the checkout request that calls `charge()` hangs, no exception is raised, nothing is logged, and the operator sees stuck workers with no error to diagnose.
findings.title: Charge call to the payment provider has no timeout

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a few attempts, with exponential backoff and jitter) and retry only transient failures (connection errors, 5xx, 429), never 4xx such as a declined card or invalid amount, which today loops forever every second. Make the POST safe to repeat by sending an idempotency key derived from `order_id` (if the provider supports one); otherwise a read timeout or 5xx returned after the provider already charged makes the retry charge the customer twice. During a provider outage, every pending checkout retries every second with no limit, a retry storm that also blocks callers forever. After the last attempt, raise an error carrying the order id and the provider's status.
findings.title: Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge, on every error

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt as a structured event (order id, attempt number, HTTP status or exception type, never the request body or credentials) and expose a counter of charge failures. Today, when the provider is down or rejects a charge, the exception is dropped: the operator has no log line, no metric and no error, and cannot tell a slow checkout from a provider outage or a declined order.
findings.title: Charge failures are swallowed without any log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or the application configuration. The task was verified against the provider's sandbox, while production must call the live endpoint: with the URL baked in, switching between sandbox and production, or pointing a test environment away from real charges, needs a code change and a release.
findings.title: Provider URL hard-coded instead of read from configuration
